dramatizationLimits: No hospital chronology, infusion, first cry, recovery mechanism or physical grief reconstruction.
No claim that leaving school was immediate or that he never returned.
Retrospective sources are memory-framed; no invented room, dialogue, meal or audition gesture.
avoidRules: Do not turn work into a cure for bereavement.
Do not claim blindness created musical talent or that help negated independence.
Short summaries are authorized exceptions to full moment and length requirements.

episode.throughLine: A short testimony-led account of bereavement, support, precarious musical work and a new engagement; no adjudication of conflicting hospital chronology or claim that employment cured grief.

contentProfile.contentNote: Maternal bereavement and food insecurity. FOR OWNER READING, not approved: user-authorized short source-led form. Remembered practical responses are summarized across 1945–1948, not a single grief-to-recovery sequence. Opening says mid-teens because interview ages vary; range 14–18 retained. Matching unchanged. Hospital, first-cry, infusion and cure claims are removed.

facts.statement: Charles was born September 23, 1930. HistoryLink places his mother's death before his fifteenth birthday; the narration uses mid-teens, preserving age uncertainty across interviews.

sourceRefs.locator: The Man, paragraph beginning Born Ray Charles Robinson; birth date only. The next paragraph's 1947 Seattle date is not adopted.
On His Own: mother died shortly before his fifteenth birthday. Combined with birth September 23, 1930. Rounded age in interviews is not controlling.

arc.canonicalText: He was in his mid-teens, away at school, when news came that his mother had died. A telegram was read to him.
arc.sourceNote: Recalled school news; no exact room or bodily action. User-authorized short source-led format; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: In his memory, the loss was so painful that he struggled to describe it to other people. He had loved her deeply.
arc.sourceNote: His attributed difficulty expressing the loss, without disputed physical chronology. User-authorized short source-led format; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: Later, he agreed to share his earnings with family friends who housed and fed him. He accepted their help.
arc.sourceNote: Remembered agreement, not a reconstructed encounter or immediate response at school. User-authorized short source-led format; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: He played with small bands, but some days he had little more than fish and crackers to eat. One group copied a successful bandleader's sound, hoping to earn money. Eventually he chose a distant city where he thought he might have a chance. He travelled there by bus.
arc.sourceNote: Clearly compressed Florida period followed by travel, not one meal or one failed audition. User-authorized short source-led format; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: In the new city, he pleaded for entry to a club and sang successfully. Two days later, he had work.
arc.sourceNote: Retrospective club account, with subsequent result visibly later; no instant cure. User-authorized short source-led format; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText: For customers, he imitated a popular singer and pianist, hoping the familiar sound would keep him employed. He was still earning through imitation.
arc.sourceNote: Local early employment, not later distinctive voice or a finished recovery. User-authorized short source-led format; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.

arc.canonicalText:
His name was Ray Charles.

He became a singer and pianist whose music joined gospel and blues.

Your life is not theirs.

But a piece of this story may still sit beside you.

You are allowed to need other people while making a choice of your own.

You do not have to feel certain about everything.
arc.sourceNote: Permission, not a recommendation to move, leave school or work through grief. User-authorized short source-led format; FOR OWNER READING, not approved.
